title: Kushner Meets Netanyahu After Hamas Talks: Will the Gaza Ceasefire Move Forward?
summary:
Imagine two sides in a big fight, and someone is trying to get them to shake hands. That's kind of what's happening in the Middle East right now. Jared Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law and a special negotiator, met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday. This was just one day after Kushner met with the leader of Hamas, the group that controls Gaza.

Here's the problem: There's a 15-point plan, called a road map, that the United States supports to make the ceasefire in Gaza work better. Hamas says it agrees to the plan, which includes giving up its weapons. But Israel says no—it wants Hamas to completely disarm BEFORE Israeli soldiers leave Gaza. So they're stuck.

A lot is at stake. About 2 million Palestinians live in Gaza, and the war has destroyed many of their homes. The road map would also help rebuild Gaza and decide who controls it in the future. But right now, Israeli forces control about 60% of Gaza, and Netanyahu has talked about taking even more.

Several countries, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, are upset with Israel for rejecting the plan. They said Israel is "obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza." That's a strong statement.

Not everyone in Gaza believes the talks will work. Mohammad Abu al-Qombuz, who lives in a tent camp in Gaza City, said, "A conference here and there, it is all lies. We need a definitive solution that would work for everybody."

Netanyahu has an election coming up on October 27, and some of his government partners are very tough on Gaza. So he might not want to make big decisions before then. Meanwhile, the anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attack that started the war is also coming up. Everyone is waiting to see what happens next.
why_it_matters: A ceasefire could help families in Gaza rebuild and live safely, and it shows how hard peace can be when each side wants different things.
